notes: Eval target is this repo's own solution (dotnet-aicraft.sln). The `dotnet aicraft` CLI is installed and runnable. Prompts are grounded in real symbols so old-vs-new skill runs are directly comparable. All prompts are read-only or --dry-run; none mutate the working tree.

evals.name: blast-radius-refs
evals.prompt: I'm about to change the constructor of the DaemonTransportException class in this .NET solution. Before I touch it I need the full blast radius: every place in the solution that references DaemonTransportException, across both src and tests. Give me the complete list with file and line.
evals.expected_output: Uses dotnet aicraft refs (discovering the FQN via symbols first if needed) rather than grep/Glob/Read. Returns the full reference set including both src/ and tests/ locations.

evals.name: call-graph-callers
evals.prompt: There's a helper method BuildTransportError inside DaemonClient. I want to understand its incoming call sites — what calls it? Show me the callers.
evals.expected_output: Uses dotnet aicraft callers (default incoming direction), resolving the FQN of DaemonClient.BuildTransportError. Does not grep for the method name.

evals.name: rename-safety
evals.prompt: I'd like to rename the method IsTransportFailure to IsTransportException across the whole solution. Is that safe, and what exactly would change? Do NOT apply anything yet — I just want to see the impact first.
evals.expected_output: Discovers the FQN (symbols), then runs rename --dry-run and reports the changes[] without applying. Does not perform a manual find/replace.

evals.name: dead-code-scan
evals.prompt: Are there any dead or unused methods in the DotnetAICraft source project (src/DotnetAICraft) that I could safely delete? I want candidates with some confidence signal, not guesses.
evals.expected_output: Uses dotnet aicraft unused (optionally narrowed to the project) and may confirm with refs. Does not attempt to infer dead code by reading files or grepping.

evals.name: defection-tool-split
evals.prompt: Two things about the ambiguous-solution error path in this .NET solution. First, I want to retire the literal error-code token "SOLUTION_AMBIGUOUS" — show me every place that exact string appears in the source so I can see the spread. Second, the method that emits it (SolutionPathResolver.Resolve) is shared, so before I touch its behaviour I need its blast radius: every caller of that method across the solution, with file and line.
evals.expected_output: Splits tools correctly rather than forcing everything through one. Part 1 (a string literal) is a legitimate grep/Search target — using text search there is correct, not a defection. Part 2 (callers of SolutionPathResolver.Resolve) must use dotnet aicraft callers (resolving the FQN), NOT grep — grep would miss the compiler-accurate call set. Failure modes: using aicraft to hunt the string literal (overreach), or using grep to find the callers (the silent-miss defection this skill targets).

evals.name: plan-uuid-command-orientation
evals.prompt: I want to add a new `uuid` command to this CLI tool — it should return a freshly generated GUID that is produced by the daemon process (not by the client). Plan the change for me: which files I'd touch, how a command is wired end to end (argument parsing → client → daemon request → daemon-side handler → response), and where exactly the GUID should be generated so it genuinely comes from the daemon. I only want the plan and the list of touch points — don't implement it.
evals.expected_output: An open-ended scoping/orientation task with NO explicit symbol question. The skill targets exactly this moment: the model should map the existing command architecture semantically — e.g. dotnet aicraft symbols --pattern "*Command*" to enumerate commands, outline on an existing command class to see its shape, refs/callers to trace command registration and the client→daemon dispatch path, describe on the daemon request handler — rather than orienting by find -name "*Command.cs" + grep + Read-ing whole files. PASS if aicraft is the primary discovery/navigation tool for understanding the command pattern and the client-daemon flow. Reading one or two files to confirm exact wiring is fine; DEFECTION = doing the structural discovery predominantly via find/Glob/grep/whole-file Reads. The plan's quality (correctly identifying parse→client→daemon→handler touch points and that the GUID must be generated daemon-side) is a secondary quality signal.
